comparison: Both evaluate basic characterization of ΔmreB phenotype (C1, C10, C11, C16, C17). OpenEval provides comprehensive coverage of C1-C18 including fitness, morphology, and complementation. Peer review focuses on subset (C1, C9-C11, C16-C17, C23-C24) and explicitly notes all reviewers acknowledge the finding without concerns.

Both address single-cell measurements of septum positioning and growth asymmetry (C28-C33). OpenEval R4 covers C28-C33 with quantitative data from Figure 1G. Peer R2 includes these claims plus C2, C151-C152 about mechanisms, explicitly noting Reviewer 3 praised the detailed microscopy investigation.

Partial overlap on viability claims C23-C24. OpenEval R3 comprehensively covers C23-C27 on live/dead assays and fitness measurements. Peer R1 includes C23-C24 as part of broader characterization, with no concerns raised about these data.

Both address fitness restoration while maintaining spherical shape (C34-C38). OpenEval R5 covers C34-C41 with detailed time-course data. Peer R3 includes C34-C38 plus C3, C139-C140, C142, explicitly noting all reviewers acknowledge this key finding and Reviewer 2 finds it interesting.

Both evaluate sequencing identification of pbp1A mutations (C42-C47, C59). OpenEval R6 covers C42-C51, C59 from whole-genome sequencing. Peer R4 includes C4, C42-C47, C59, C141, with Reviewer 3 explicitly listing this as a leading result and noting no concerns about sequencing data.

Strong agreement on reconstruction experiments (C60-C66). OpenEval R8 comprehensively covers C60-C66 with microscopy, fitness, and double mutant data. Peer R5 covers C5, C60-C66, with Reviewer 1 confirming reconstruction experiments were sufficient and convincing.

Strong agreement on pbp1A mutations in wild-type background (C67-C72). OpenEval R9 covers C67-C73 including growth curves and width measurements. Peer R10 includes C18, C67-C72, noting this is part of genetic reconstruction confirming loss-of-function, not questioned by reviewers.

Strong agreement on biophysical analysis of added volume (C92-C97). OpenEval R11 covers C89-C97 with theoretical framework and measurements. Peer R11 includes C22, C92-C97, noting this is part of the 'impressively detailed investigation' praised by Reviewer 3.

Partial overlap on elongation/septation rate imbalance (C105-C108). OpenEval R12 comprehensively covers C98-C109 on size homeostasis mechanisms. Peer R6 includes C105-C108, C110-C111, C115, C171-C172, C174, with Reviewer 3 explicitly stating fitness recovery reduces variability in cell volume.

Partial overlap on Cg/Cs measurements (C110-C111, C115). OpenEval R13 covers C110-C124 on elongation symmetry as primary fitness determinant. Peer R6 includes these claims as part of broader mechanism connecting mutations to reduced variability, explicitly supported by Reviewer 3.

Strong agreement on peptidoglycan analysis and TPase activity (C125-C131). OpenEval R14 covers C125-C132 with biochemical data. Peer R7 includes C125-C131, C154, C169, with Reviewer 3 explicitly listing TPase reduction as a leading result, no concerns raised about biochemical data.

Strong agreement on FDAA labeling showing heterogeneous synthesis (C133-C138). OpenEval R15 covers C133-C138 comparing to E. coli. Peer R8 includes C133-C138, C155-C156, with Reviewer 1 noting this increases understanding of MreB's role in cell wall synthesis homogeneity.

Partial overlap on time-lapse microscopy of aspect ratio (C19-C21). OpenEval R2 covers C19-C22 on morphology and elongation rates. Peer R13 includes C19-C21, C41 as part of detailed characterization of division patterns, not questioned by reviewers.

Partial overlap on alternative evolutionary routes (C74, C76-C78, C80). OpenEval R10 comprehensively covers C74-C88 on ftsEX mutations and complex phenotypes. Peer R9 includes C48-C51, C74, C76-C78, C80, acknowledging alternative routes as part of 'impressively detailed investigation.'

Partial overlap on fitness restoration claims (C139-C140, C142). OpenEval R16 covers C139-C145 on fitness measurements and reconstruction. Peer R3 includes C3, C34-C38, C139-C140, C142, with all reviewers explicitly acknowledging rapid fitness restoration.

Minimal overlap on mechanistic inference (C151-C152). OpenEval R17 covers C146-C153 on differential elongation as primary cause. Peer R2 includes C2, C28-C33, C151-C152 as part of single-cell analysis praised by Reviewer 3.

Minimal overlap on competing hypotheses (C154, C169). OpenEval R18 covers C154-C169 presenting two hypotheses about TPase activity. Peer R7 includes C125-C131, C154, C169, with Reviewer 3 supporting the TPase reduction mechanism.
